name: SortableList
description: A list put in order by hand — a playlist, the columns of a report, a set of priorities.

props.name: children
props.description: The items: `SortableList.Item`s, each with a `value`, rendered in the order the app holds.

props.name: onOrderChange
props.description: The new order, as the items' `value`s. Fires once for a drop and on every step the keyboard takes, so the list moves as the arrows do. The app owns the order: render the items in it and the list follows.

props.name: onOrderCommit
props.description: The order once it has settled — a drop, or Enter after the arrows. The one to save.

props.name: tag
props.description: `ol` when the order means something — steps, a ranking. Default `ul`.

parts.name: SortableList.Item
parts.description: One item in the order: a `List.Item` that knows who it is.

props.name: value
props.description: Who the item is in the order `onOrderChange` reports. Unique within the list.

props.name: label
props.description: What the handle and the announcements call the item: "Move Ada Lovelace". Defaults to `value`.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Leaves the item where it is: its handle is disabled. Others may still move past it.

props.name: children
props.description: The item's parts: `List.Media`, `List.Content`, `List.End`, `List.Actions` — or anything at all, in one row.

props.name: size
props.description: The item's spacing. Default `md`, at least 56px tall; `sm` is 44px, still a finger's width; `lg` is 72px.

props.name: wrap
props.description: Lets the item's parts wrap onto a second line when they do not fit, instead of squeezing.

props.name: selected
props.description: Tints the item as chosen. The state a reader hears belongs on the control that chose it — a checkbox, `aria-pressed`.

props.name: chevron
props.description: Ends the item with a chevron: pressing it goes somewhere with more. Decoration, so `aria-hidden`.

props.name: children
props.description: What the handle shows. Six dots unless given something else; its name is "Move" and the item's `label` either way.

keyboard.action: Picks the item up, and drops it again.
Moves a held item one place. Home and End move it to either end.
Puts a held item back where it was picked up from.

a11y: Dragging is not a keyboard gesture, so the keyboard gets a **grab**: Enter or Space on a handle picks the item up, the arrows move it, Enter drops it and Escape puts it back — DashboardGrid's model. Every step is announced in a polite live region that is there before there is anything to say.
A press on a handle that does not drag picks the item up too, and while one is held a press on any other item drops it there — the single-pointer way to reorder that WCAG 2.5.7 asks a drag to have.
